actions.action: Check soil moisture with a finger or by lifting the pot
Check whether the pot has drainage holes
Scoop out the mold and 1-2 cm of topsoil and replace with fresh potting mix
Remove dead leaves from the soil surface
Water only when the top 2-3 cm of soil are dry
Empty water from the saucer or outer pot
Move the plant to a brighter spot
Improve airflow with a small fan or an open window
If decline continues, slide the plant out and inspect the roots
Trim brown or mushy roots if found
Repot in fresh well-draining mix in a pot with drainage holes
Optionally dust cinnamon on the soil surface
Optionally drench the soil with diluted 3% hydrogen peroxide

reason: The answer correctly identifies mold caused by overly wet soil, but its main advice is to replace only the topsoil and let it dry, with a full soil change offered only as a conditional repot; nothing it recommends is harmful.
